title: TCP Three-Way Handshake
misconceptions: The initial SYN packet carries application payload data.
Two packets are sufficient to reliably establish a full-duplex connection.
Initial sequence numbers always begin at zero for every connection.
The final ACK packet requires an explicit acknowledgment back from the server before connection establishment.

rubric.text: Explains that the primary purpose of the handshake is establishing a reliable connection prior to data exchange.
States that the client initiates the handshake by transmitting a packet with the SYN flag set.
Explains that the client generates a pseudo-random initial sequence number rather than starting at zero.
Clarifies that the initial SYN packet does not carry application payload data.
States that the server responds with a single packet carrying both SYN and ACK flags.
Explains that the acknowledgment number sent by the server equals the client sequence number incremented by one.
States that the client concludes the handshake procedure by transmitting a packet with the ACK flag set.
Explains that three distinct messages are mathematically required to verify bidirectional reachability across an unreliable network.
